Simulate a population evolving on an adaptive landscape

Source: R/simulate.R
simulate_population.Rd

Individual-based simulation with discrete, non-overlapping generations: selection (parents sampled with fitness-dependent weights), reproduction, mutation, then development of new genotypes into phenotypes.

Usage

simulate_population(
  model,
  landscape,
  start = NULL,
  start_genotype = NULL,
  N = 1000,
  generations = 10000,
  mu = 0.01,
  sigma = 0.05,
  ploidy = 1,
  reproduction = c("clonal", "sexual"),
  sexes = TRUE,
  selection = selection_relative_min(),
  lower = 0,
  upper = Inf,
  invalid = c("lethal", "reject"),
  record_every = 10,
  record_m = FALSE,
  stop = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  dev_args = list()
)

Arguments

model

A `grn` model.

landscape

Function from a phenotype matrix to fitness values.

start

Starting phenotype (trait values). The population starts monomorphic at the genotype found by [genotype_at()].

start_genotype

Alternatively, the starting genotypic values.

N

Population size.

generations

Maximum number of generations.

mu

Per-allele mutation rate per locus.

sigma

Standard deviation of mutational effects (scalar or per locus).

ploidy

1 or 2.

reproduction

`"clonal"` or `"sexual"`.

sexes

For sexual reproduction, split the population into equal numbers of females and males.

selection

A selection scheme, see [selection].

lower, upper

Bounds on allelic values.

invalid

What happens to individuals whose development fails (no stable steady state): `"lethal"` gives them zero weight; `"reject"` (clonal only) discards the mutation that caused the failure.

record_every

Record population summaries every this many generations (the first and last generations are always recorded).

record_m

Also record the M-matrix at the mean genotype.

stop

Optional stopping rule, see [stop_at_peaks()].

seed

Optional RNG seed.

dev_args

List of extra arguments for [develop()].

Value

An object of class `grn_sim`: a list with `trajectory` (data frame of generation, trait means, phenotypic (co)variances `P_*`, mean fitness and number of failed developments; plus `M_*` if `record_m`), `outcome` (index of the peak reached, or `NA`), `generations` run, and `final` (alleles, genotypes, phenotypes and fitness of the last generation). With clonal reproduction and no environmental noise the phenotypic covariance matrix equals the genetic covariance matrix G.

Details

Each locus has `ploidy` allele copies; the genotypic value of a locus is the sum of its alleles. Mutations hit each allele copy with probability `mu` per generation and add a normal deviate with sd `sigma`; allelic values are kept within `[lower, upper]`.

With `reproduction = "clonal"` offspring copy their parent. With `"sexual"`, each offspring has two parents (a female and a male if `sexes = TRUE`), and inherits at each locus one randomly chosen allele copy from each parent (free recombination; for haploids, the allele comes from either parent).

The original analysis scripts correspond to `ploidy = 1`, `reproduction = "clonal"`, `selection = selection_relative_min()`, `mu = 0.01`, `sigma = 0.05`, `N = 1000`.
